references.text: God establishes his covenant with Abraham and his descendants, promising to be their God—the same covenant confirmed in Deuteronomy 29:12
God promises to take Israel as his people and be their God, the same covenant relationship described in Deuteronomy 29:12
Israel shall be God's treasured possession among all peoples, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation
God promises to dwell among the people, be their God, and they shall be his people
God confirms the oath he swore to Abraham, as mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:12
God repeats the promise given to Jacob that was first made to Abraham and Isaac, the three patriarchs mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:12
Jeremiah prophesies about the new covenant where God will be their God and they shall be his people
Ezekiel restates the covenant formula: you shall be my people, and I will be your God
The book of Hebrews quotes the covenant formula from the new covenant that God will be their God and they shall be his people
Paul quotes the covenant formula that God will dwell among them, be their God, and they shall be his people
The final fulfillment of the covenant promise: God will dwell with humanity, they shall be his people, and he will be their God
